```{r}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Simple Metropolis-Hastings MCMC Implementation
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

known_params <- c(
  V = 1000,      # Lake volume (m³)
  Q = 50,        # Inflow/outflow rate (m³/day)
  C_in=5
)

# We'll implement a simple Metropolis-Hastings algorithm
# This helps students understand the mechanics before using packages

metropolis_mcmc <- function(
    n_iter = 10000,           # Number of iterations
    initial_k = 0.3,          # Starting value
    proposal_sd = 0.05,       # Proposal step size
    observations,              # Data
    known_params,              # Known parameters
    prior_range = c(0.01, 1)  # Prior range for k
) {
  
  # Storage for chain
  chain <- data.frame(
    iteration = 1:n_iter,
    k = NA,
    log_likelihood = NA,
    accepted = FALSE
  )
  
  # Initialize
  current_k <- initial_k
  current_params <- c(known_params, k = current_k)
  
  # Calculate initial likelihood
  out <- ode(y = c(C = observations$C_obs[1]),
             times = observations$time,
             func = cstr_model,
             parms = current_params)
  out_df <- as.data.frame(out)
  
  # Log-likelihood (assuming normal errors)
  errors <- observations$C_obs - out_df$C
  current_loglik <- -length(errors)/2 * log(2*pi) - 
                    0.5 * sum((errors/0.2)^2)  # Assume SD = 0.2
  
  chain[1, ] <- c(1, current_k, current_loglik, TRUE)
  
  # MCMC loop
  for (i in 2:n_iter) {
    # Propose new k
    proposed_k <- rnorm(1, current_k, proposal_sd)
    
    # Check prior bounds
    if (proposed_k >= prior_range[1] && proposed_k <= prior_range[2]) {
      
      # Run model with proposed k
      proposed_params <- c(known_params, k = proposed_k)
      out <- ode(y = c(C = observations$C_obs[1]),
                 times = observations$time,
                 func = cstr_model,
                 parms = proposed_params)
      out_df <- as.data.frame(out)
      
      # Calculate log-likelihood
      errors <- observations$C_obs - out_df$C
      proposed_loglik <- -length(errors)/2 * log(2*pi) - 
                         0.5 * sum((errors/0.2)^2)
      
      # Metropolis acceptance ratio
      log_ratio <- proposed_loglik - current_loglik
      
      if (log(runif(1)) < log_ratio) {
        # Accept
        current_k <- proposed_k
        current_loglik <- proposed_loglik
        accepted <- TRUE
      } else {
        # Reject
        accepted <- FALSE
      }
    } else {
      # Outside prior - reject automatically
      accepted <- FALSE
      proposed_loglik <- -Inf
    }
    
    # Store
    chain[i, ] <- c(i, current_k, current_loglik, accepted)
  }
  
  return(chain)
}

# Run MCMC
n_iter <- 10000
mcmc_chain <- metropolis_mcmc(
  n_iter = n_iter,
  initial_k = 0.3,
  proposal_sd = 0.03,
  observations = observations,
  known_params = known_params
)

# Calculate acceptance rate
acceptance_rate <- mean(mcmc_chain$accepted)
cat("MCMC Acceptance rate:", round(100 * acceptance_rate, 1), "%\n")

```

```{r}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SIMPLE METROPOLIS-HASTINGS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

simple_mcmc <- function(data, n_iter = 10000) {
  chain <- numeric(n_iter)
  current_k <- 0.3
  
  # Pre-compute ODE for current_k 
  params <- c(Q = 1, V = 10, C_in = 1, k = current_k)
  out <- ode(y = c(C = 0), times = data$time, func = cstr_model, parms = params)
  current_error <- sum((data$C_obs - out[, "C"])^2)
  
  for (i in 1:n_iter) {
    # Propose new k
    proposed_k <- current_k + rnorm(1, 0, 0.03)
    
    # Keep in bounds
    if (proposed_k < 0.01 || proposed_k > 1) {
      chain[i] <- current_k
      next
    }
    
    # Run ODE with proposed k
    params["k"] <- proposed_k
    out <- ode(y = c(C = 0), times = data$time, func = cstr_model, parms = params)
    proposed_error <- sum((data$C_obs - out[, "C"])^2)
    
    # Accept or reject
    if (runif(1) < exp(-(proposed_error - current_error)/0.01)) {
      current_k <- proposed_k
      current_error <- proposed_error
    }
    
    chain[i] <- current_k
  }
  
  return(chain)
}

# Run it
posterior_k <- simple_mcmc(observations)

# Visualize
hist(posterior_k[2000:10000], breaks = 50, main = "Posterior for k",
     xlab = "Decay rate k", col = "steelblue")

```

```{r}
library(rstan)

# Stan code with ODE integration
stan_code <- "
functions {
  real[] cstr_model(real t, real[] y, real[] params, real[] x_r, int[] x_i) {
    real k = params[1];
    real C = y[1];
    real dC_dt = -k * C;
    return {dC_dt};
  }
}
data {
  int<lower=0> N;
  real t0;
  real ts[N];
  real y_obs[N];
}
parameters {
  real<lower=0, upper=1> k;
  real<lower=0> sigma;
}
model {
  real y_hat[N, 1];
  real y0[1] = {y_obs[1]};
  
  // Priors
  k ~ beta(1, 1);
  sigma ~ exponential(1);
  
  // Solve ODE
  y_hat = integrate_ode_rk45(cstr_model, y0, t0, ts, {k}, rep_array(0.0, 0), rep_array(0, 0));
  
  // Likelihood
  for (i in 1:N) {
    y_obs[i] ~ normal(y_hat[i, 1], sigma);
  }
}
"

# Fit the model
fit <- stan(model_code = stan_code, 
            data = list(N = nrow(observations), 
                        t0 = 0, 
                        ts = observations$time, 
                        y_obs = observations$C_obs),
            iter = 2000, chains = 4)
```
